warrantyCautions: Current handbook: vehicle 6 years / 150,000 km; power battery and drive unit 8 years / 160,000 km. Confirm the updated terms against the VIN and first-registration date.

Australian reporting says the April 2025 simplified warranty was backdated to deliveries from August 2022. The current booklet alone does not establish each older VIN’s amendment: obtain written BYD confirmation before relying on removal of the original component carve-outs.
Battery retention threshold is 70%; an eligible remedy may use a repaired, new, reconditioned or remanufactured unit. Normal wear, impact and flood damage are excluded.

Current booklet: auxiliary lead-acid battery and emergency AC/discharge cable have 12-month limits (auxiliary battery also 20,000 km). The warranty follows the car, with maintenance records required; Queensland timing generally starts at first registration, including an earlier demonstrator registration.

Current 2026 handbook also excludes vehicles acquired at auction or imported outside BYD Australia. This wording's application to a used car's ownership history is not resolved here: obtain written VIN-specific coverage confirmation if auction/grey-import history exists.

expertReviews.scope: Australian manufacturer-hosted first drive. Article covers both variants but explicitly only Premium was driven; no child-restraint installation or long-term reliability trial. Some embedded spec/warranty entries conflict with official documents and are not adopted.
expertReviews.verdict: More appealing handling and cabin; ride firmness remains a compromise.
positiveThemes: Improved driving composure and a less cluttered console.
Competitive equipment and larger Premium luggage capacity.
negativeThemes: Firm reactions to some bumps and limited steering feedback.
Climate controls still require the touchscreen.
